courses.name: Introduction to Programming
courses.description: This course introduces fundamental programming concepts using a high-level language. Topics include variables, data types, control structures, functions, arrays, and basic input/output. Students will learn problem-solving techniques and develop basic programming skills through hands-on labs and assignments.

courses.name: Object-Oriented Programming
courses.description: This course covers object-oriented programming principles including encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction. Students will learn to design and implement classes, work with interfaces, exception handling, and file I/O. Emphasis on software design patterns and best practices.

courses.name: Data Structures and Algorithms
courses.description: Fundamental data structures including arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, graphs, and hash tables. Algorithm analysis using Big-O notation. Sorting and searching algorithms. Recursion and dynamic programming. Students implement data structures and analyze algorithm efficiency.

courses.name: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science
courses.description: Mathematical foundations for computer science including logic, set theory, functions, relations, proof techniques, combinatorics, graph theory, and discrete probability. Applications to algorithms, cryptography, and computer science theory.

courses.name: Computer Organization and Architecture
courses.description: Computer system organization including CPU architecture, memory hierarchy, instruction sets, addressing modes, pipelining, and parallel processing. Assembly language programming. Performance evaluation and benchmarks.

courses.name: Operating Systems
courses.description: Operating system concepts including process management, scheduling, synchronization, deadlocks, memory management, file systems, and I/O systems. Case studies of modern operating systems. Students implement OS components in projects.

courses.name: Database Systems
courses.description: Database design and management including ER modeling, relational model, SQL, normalization, transaction processing, concurrency control, recovery, and database security. Introduction to NoSQL and distributed databases. Practical database design projects.

courses.name: Software Engineering
courses.description: Software development life cycle, requirements engineering, design patterns, testing strategies, version control, project management, and agile methodologies. Team-based software project applying engineering principles.

courses.name: Computer Networks
courses.description: Network architectures, protocols, and standards. OSI and TCP/IP models. Physical, data link, network, transport, and application layers. Routing, switching, wireless networks, network security, and socket programming.

courses.name: Theory of Computation
courses.description: Automata theory, formal languages, and computability. Finite automata, regular expressions, context-free grammars, pushdown automata, Turing machines, decidability, and complexity classes (P, NP, NP-complete).

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Fundamental AI concepts including search algorithms, knowledge representation, reasoning, machine learning basics, neural networks, natural language processing, and AI ethics. Practical implementations of AI techniques.

courses.name: Compiler Design
courses.description: Compiler structure, lexical analysis, parsing techniques (top-down, bottom-up), syntax-directed translation, intermediate code generation, code optimization, and code generation. Students build a compiler for a subset of a programming language.

courses.name: Computer Graphics
courses.description: Graphics hardware, 2D/3D transformations, viewing, clipping, rendering pipelines, shading models, texture mapping, ray tracing, and animation. OpenGL programming. Mathematical foundations for computer graphics.

courses.name: Web Programming
courses.description: Web technologies including HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, front-end frameworks (React/Vue), back-end development (Node.js, databases), RESTful APIs, authentication, deployment, and web security. Full-stack web application development.

courses.name: Mobile Application Development
courses.description: Mobile app development for iOS and Android platforms. Native development (Swift/Kotlin), cross-platform frameworks (Flutter/React Native), UI/UX design, mobile databases, sensors, location services, and app deployment.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.description: Supervised and unsupervised learning algorithms including regression, classification, clustering, dimensionality reduction, neural networks, deep learning, model evaluation, and deployment. Python libraries (scikit-learn, TensorFlow/PyTorch).

courses.name: Cybersecurity Fundamentals
courses.description: Security principles, cryptography, network security, application security, vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, security policies, and ethical hacking. Hands-on labs with security tools.

courses.name: Distributed Systems
courses.description: Distributed system architectures, communication, synchronization, consistency, fault tolerance, distributed algorithms, consensus, replication, and case studies of modern distributed systems (Hadoop, Spark, blockchain).

courses.name: Senior Project I
courses.description: First semester of capstone project. Students propose, design, and begin implementation of a significant software system. Requirements analysis, system design, project planning, and prototype development. Technical writing and presentation skills.

courses.name: Senior Project II
courses.description: Second semester of capstone project. Continuation of CSCI480: implementation, testing, deployment, and documentation of the software system. Final presentation and demo. Professional practices and ethics.

courses.name: Special Topics in Computer Science
courses.description: Advanced topics not covered in regular curriculum. Content varies by semester based on faculty expertise and student interest. May include emerging technologies, research areas, or industry trends. Repeatable for credit with different topics.

courses.name: Internship in Computer Science
courses.description: Supervised work experience in computer science field. Students apply academic knowledge in professional setting. Requires faculty sponsorship, learning objectives, work logs, and final report. Minimum 120 hours of work.
